title: Turn 3: deploy the token maker or hold for a protected Zada?

board.you: Turn 3, precombat main. Battlefield: Skirk Prospector, two Mountains and Goblin Burrows untapped (3 mana). Hand: Dragon Fodder, Brightstone Ritual, Zada, Hedron Grinder, Swiftfoot Boots, Mountain. Zada is castable next turn on curve (goldfish mean cast turn 4.35, 70% of games exactly turn 4).
board.table: Player 2 (Golgari midrange) holds two mana open with a deathtouch blocker. Player 3 (Azorius control, the table's known sweeper deck — assume it holds up 4+ mana for a wrath by turn 5-6) just tapped low for a draw spell. Player 4 (Selesnya tokens) has five tokens and an anthem and is currently the table's visible threat.

scenario.question: Do you cast Dragon Fodder now and develop wide — signaling the engine a turn early — or hold everything to land Zada with ritual or Boots protection?

branches.choice: Cast Dragon Fodder now, land Zada on schedule next turn
branches.line: Precombat: Dragon Fodder ('Create two 1/1 red Goblin creature tokens'), play the Mountain, pass with Prospector plus two tokens. Turn 4: Zada on schedule — 70% of goldfish games do exactly this — and pass, holding Brightstone Ritual.
branches.signals: Two 1/1s beside a Prospector read as chump blockers to the Golgari deck, not an engine. The Selesnya board keeps the table's eyes where you want them. Zada on turn 4 with no cantrip shown looks like a mediocre 3/3.
branches.coalition_risk: Low this turn. The token deck at five bodies plus anthem is the lightning rod — nobody wastes a wrath on three Goblins.
branches.coaching: This is the line the deck is built for, so play it proudly. Goldfish mean bodies on turn 3 is only 2.36 — Dragon Fodder puts you above curve exactly when it's cheapest, and 'early token maker drawn' averages turn 3.18, so this is the scripted tempo. Every body multiplies the engine: verified stack 001 shows four Goblins turning one Crimson Wisps into five cards, and each body grows Brightstone Ritual ('Add {R} for each Goblin on the battlefield') for the turn you go off. Hold tokens in hand and you make Zada, the Ritual, and the future cantrip all worse at once.

branches.choice: Hold everything; pass with three mana up
branches.line: Play the Mountain and pass with all mana open, representing interaction. Turn 4: Zada, with Brightstone Ritual held as an instant-speed mana burst for a follow-up.
branches.signals: A mono-red deck that has shown one Prospector passing on full mana reads as a bluff or a slow hand. Golgari may probe with an attack, and the Azorius player books you as low priority.
branches.coalition_risk: Medium. An unexplained hold from the red deck invites testing, and you fall behind the token deck's board for nothing — Brightstone Ritual counts Goblins on the battlefield, and with one Goblin out it adds almost nothing.
branches.coaching: You're holding a ritual whose value you refuse to build. Yes, Brightstone Ritual is an instant, so you can legally hold it for any priority window — but the card scales with the exact board you're declining to make. You keep Zada on the same schedule as the aggressive line while shrinking every payoff attached to her. This line only makes sense if you're representing removal you don't have, and that bluff bills you in real tempo.

citations.quote: A player may cast an instant spell any time they have priority. A player may cast a noninstant spell during their main phase any time they have priority and the stack is empty.

branches.line: Turn 3: Dragon Fodder. Turn 4: Swiftfoot Boots plus a land. Turn 5: Zada. Turn 6: equip ({1}) and fire a cantrip behind hexproof.
branches.signals: Boots before the commander telegraph 'my commander must survive to matter.' Experienced tables pre-answer Zada the moment she's cast, or hold exile removal for the equip window.
branches.coalition_risk: Low early, high late. By the time the protected engine turns on, the table no longer forgives it — and the Azorius wrath window (4+ mana held, turns 5-6) arrives before your engine does.
branches.coaching: The math calls this too slow, and the math is on your side when you listen. 'Zada online with a cantrip drawn' already averages turn 5.27 and lands by turn 6 in only 49.6% of games — push Zada to turn 5 and the engine slides to turn 6-7, where your land-drop rate has fallen to 54% and the sweeper deck has banked two full turns of held mana. Boots protect Zada after she's proven she must die, not as a precondition for casting her. Protection paid for before anyone shows a threat is tempo donated to the table.

recommendation.choice: Cast Dragon Fodder now, land Zada on schedule next turn
recommendation.rationale: Every payoff in this hand is denominated in Goblins on the battlefield — Zada's copies (stack 001: bodies equal extra cards), Brightstone Ritual (mana per Goblin), even the eventual wide attack. Two 1/1 tokens on turn 3 carry near-zero threat signal at a table watching a five-token Selesnya board, so you buy the engine's fuel at the exact moment it's free. The goldfish curve — 2.36 bodies turn 3, Zada turn 4.35, engine turn 5.27 — is the deck's winning script. Both holding lines delay the script without buying real protection.
